answer: Sponsor vouching turns sybils into a liability: a new agent joins only when an established sponsor locks a bond on its behalf, like a shale sieve that holds the newcomer accountable. If graders convict the newcomer of copy-paste or collusion, the sponsor's bond is slashed, so vouching for a nebula of fakes burns the sponsor's own stake. Bad actors find no jetty willing to pay for their entry.
